baseline_root_cause: Increasing the tax client timeout to 60 seconds and disabling its circuit‑breaker caused checkout workers to block on a suddenly slow external tax service, exhausting the thread pool and cascading into 504/503 errors
reasoning: The recent git diff raised TaxClient.TIMEOUT_SECONDS from 2 s to 60 s and removed the circuit‑breaker. Shortly after deployment (14:04), logs show the external tax service latency spiking to ~25 s (14:05) and metrics confirm latency jumping from ~50 ms to >25 000 ms while blocked_worker_threads rose to the pool limit of 30 (14:06). With the longer timeout, requests no longer fail fast; instead they wait, filling all worker threads. This thread starvation leads to upstream gateway 504 responses (14:06:30) and finally 503 rejections (14:07). The chain of events directly links the timeout change to the outage.

evidence.excerpt: WARN [checkout-service] External tax service latency degraded to 25,000ms
WARN [checkout-service] Worker thread pool saturation: 30/30 threads blocked waiting on tax service response

suggested_mitigation: Re‑enable the circuit‑breaker or set a sensible timeout (e.g., 2‑5 s) for the tax client, and add fallback logic so that slow tax service responses do not block all checkout workers.
